escalated_scenario: fire in each floor's east office plus a second alarm on each other floor
escalated_rules_checked: alert set contains the floor above and below every alarming floor
staging is the first non-alerted floor at or below FIRE_STAGING_BELOW under the fire, never an alerted floor
a staging move below the sourced rule is tagged [team-proposed, validate] in the card line's detail and basis
rules_checked: alert set contains the fire floor, the floor above and the floor below
staging exactly FIRE_STAGING_BELOW floors below the fire (exterior when that is below floor 1)
relocation floors at least FIRE_RELOCATE_MIN_BELOW below, never alert, staging or floor 1
evacuation stair differs from the attack stair
stair enclosures at least STAIR_MIN_SEP_FT apart at their nearest points
no line executes anything; every human decision names FSD or IC; AI role is evidence only
decision-support banner and SYNTHETIC flag present
firefighting-water watch only below the fire and ranked by path score
battery-room hazard always listed; 'near' exactly when within ESS_NEAR_FLOORS
fire department elevator only when the fire is at or above FIRE_LIFT_MIN_FIRE_FLOOR, exit FIRE_LIFT_EXIT_BELOW below
elevator recall stated as conditional on a lobby or hoistway detector
an impairment on an alert or relocation floor is the first hazard

rules.meaning: voice alarm reaches at least the floor above the alarming floor
rules.note: IBC 2021 907.5.2.2: 'at least the alarming floor, the floor above and the floor below'; LAFD high-rise sequence policy footnote a says the same for new high-rises

rules.meaning: voice alarm reaches at least the floor below the alarming floor
fire department staging at least this many floors below the fire floor
rules.note: Sacramento Regional Fire guideline (reviewed 08/21/22): 'Staging a minimum of two floors below'. California regional guideline, not an LAFD SOP

rules.meaning: hose line connects to the standpipe in the attack stair this many floors below the fire
rules.note: Sacramento guideline: 'Equipment should be placed outside fire attack stairwell one floor below'; IBC 905.4 puts a hose connection at every floor landing

rules.meaning: crews leave the fire service elevator at least this many floors below the fire
rules.note: Sacramento guideline: 'crews exit a minimum of two floors below'; Phase II is fire department only

rules.meaning: fire department elevator use expected only when the fire floor is at or above this level
rules.note: Sacramento guideline: 'Elevator use is authorized for fires above the sixth floor'; below that the card says stairs expected

rules.meaning: highest relocation floor is at least this many floors below the fire floor (below the staging floor)
rules.note: NIST TN 1664 reports an 'evacuate down three floors' message in a real high-rise fire; not a code rule. The building's approved Emergency Plan overrides this

rules.meaning: number of relocation floors offered to occupants of the alert floors
rules.note: sized so the design load of three alert floors fits; validate with the Emergency Plan relocation areas

rules.meaning: floors above the alert zone whose shaft and core readings are watched for smoke spread
rules.note: NISTIR 89-4035: stairwells and elevator shafts frequently become smoke-logged (stack effect). The band width is our choice

rules.meaning: an alarm this many floors or more above the fire floor is treated as possible upward spread (escalation trigger E2)
rules.note: First Interstate 1988 spread upward from floor 12 to floor 16

rules.meaning: IBC business occupant load factor used for the design occupant load (a code design figure, not a headcount)
rules.note: Jensen Hughes memo, 2023-12-01: IBC 2018+ business load factor changed from 100 to 150 sq ft per person

rules.meaning: high-rise exit stair enclosures at least 30 ft apart (or 1/4 of the diagonal), measured between the nearest points of the enclosures
rules.note: IBC 403.5.1 summary; scissor stairs count as one stairway. The synthetic layout is checked against this but no IBC compliance is claimed

rules.meaning: stair pressurization range (0.10-0.35 in. water) that the listed smoke-control system maintains
stair cameras on every 5th floor landing, viewable from the fire control room
rules.note: LAFD Requirement No. 10, Option 2 EHLF Equivalency only. Not a general high-rise requirement

rules.meaning: IBC 403 height triggers (highest occupied floor above fire department access)
an energy storage (battery) room within this many floors of the fire is flagged 'near'
rules.note: UL FSRI Surprise AZ 2019 report recommends remote gas monitoring; the distance is our choice

rules.meaning: hop limit on the water graph when predicting where firefighting water migrates
rules.note: path score cut uses the existing REACH_MIN threshold of cascade.building.rules
